requestedActions.title: List active task titles, including paginated results

guide.summary: Todoist documents OAuth2 authorization-code access for external apps to obtain user-authorized API tokens. The data:read scope grants read-only access to application data including tasks, and GET /api/v1/tasks returns active tasks with cursor pagination (limit default 50, max 200, next_cursor until null). Customers connecting their own accounts can use this path. App registration, client credentials, redirect URL configuration and token exchange are setup prerequisites. Provider review, marketplace distribution and customer-organization admin approval are not covered by the supplied snapshots and remain unknown.

findings.title: OAuth2 authorization code flow issues user-authorized API tokens
findings.detail: External applications obtain a user-authorized API token through the OAuth2 protocol. The flow redirects users to the authorization endpoint with client_id, scope and state, then exchanges the returned code at the token endpoint. Refresh tokens are enabled by default for newly created apps.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their individual Todoist accounts to the app.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels and filters. It is the least-privilege documented scope for listing active task titles and does not permit create, update, complete or delete operations.

steps.title: Read the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with a limit and the customer's Bearer token to list active task titles from the first page. Expected success is HTTP 200 with a results array of tasks, each with a content field holding the task title, plus next_cursor. Safe nonmutating boundary check: confirm the call performs only GET and that a create, update, complete or delete attempt is not made.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns results with content titles and a next_cursor value (or null if no further pages).

steps.title: Fetch the next page of active tasks using next_cursor
steps.detail: If next_cursor from the first response is not null, repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with the same limit and append cursor=<NEXT_CURSOR> from the prior response. Keep the same parameters, and continue until next_cursor is null. Do not invent a cursor or assume an empty-page stop.
steps.doneWhen: Each page returns HTTP 200 and the loop stops only when next_cursor is null; the full set of task titles has been collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
